answers.core: It's a modification to an existing `Node`, which is not doable even with a GDExtension without workarounds like using methods to set the properties.
answers.workaround: Any built-in `Control` Node can use a single script that simulates this behavior (although it would slightly change the approach from simply setting the position to calling a method that handles the interpolation), but when a `Node` that inherits `Control` is desired with custom behavior, either the animation or `Node` behavior has to be rewritten. It's not necessarily difficult, but repetitive and cumbersome.

title: Animated Control Nodes for advanced UIs
